corrections.source_says: Use null for the separately reported analyzed-person count. The paper reports twenty participants selected and then randomized, forty final design solutions evaluated, and an experiment involving 20 novice designers, but does not explicitly state a participant denominator for the expert-rating statistical analysis or a post-exclusion total. The form itself acknowledges that no separate post-exclusion total is stated; 20 should not be presented as an explicitly reported analysis count. The experiment still necessarily falls below the 50-person threshold.

Section 4.2 reports Bonferroni comparisons of Human versus ChatGPT and Human versus Midjourney, both p < 0.01. The cost results therefore describe an adverse aspect of the AI-assisted designs.

confirmed: The stored source is arXiv:2502.00283v1, dated 1 Feb 2025 on PDF p. 1, and contains 20 pages; the title and six authors match the form (p. 1). The entire markdown conversion, including references, was read.

Random assignment of people to ChatGPT, Midjourney, Combined, or Human groups is explicit; this is one experiment with two tasks, not two independent participant samples (p. 5, Sections 3.1-3.2). has_randomized_people_study=true.

The lab_rct design classification fits the described training and timed experimental procedure; this is human AI-assistance research, with context_class=none rather than ai_vs_human or observational (pp. 5-6, Section 3.2; codebook Sections 3-4).

Twenty novice designers were selected before random allocation; the conclusion also describes an experiment involving 20 novice designers. There cannot be 50 analyzed participants in this experiment, so criterion_2=not_met and core=no are correct (p. 5, Sections 3.1-3.2; p. 16, Section 6).

Forty final design solutions were assessed by five professional designers using a seven-point scale. Outputs and assessors must not be counted as additional randomized participants (p. 7, Section 3.3.2).

The tasks were baby-chair and tangible-music-brick designs, 20 minutes each, with an image and essential text descriptions for each task. The tools were GPT-3.5 and Midjourney; no Midjourney version is specified (p. 4, Sections 2.2-3; pp. 5-6, Section 3.2).
The novelty reported string is exact: Midjourney 4.60 (SD 1.23), Human 3.20 (SD 1.17), with Bonferroni pairwise p < 0.01; Table 3 combines both tasks (p. 10, Section 4.2; p. 11, Table 3).

The overall-design-performance reported string is exact: Midjourney 4.34 (SD 0.75), Human 3.59 (SD 0.71), with pairwise p = 0.01. Overall design performance is not explicitly labeled overall creativity (p. 11, Section 4.2 and Table 3). The one-line finding reproduces these novelty and overall figures correctly.
The paper also reports Combined novelty 4.90 (SD 1.31), with p < 0.01 versus Human, and ChatGPT overall performance 4.24 (SD 0.60), with p = 0.02 versus Human (pp. 10-11, Section 4.2 and Table 3).

The exact statistical analysis unit and rating-aggregation method are not specified; retaining null for the outcome analysis unit and its n_units avoids treating designs or individual expert ratings as independent people (p. 7, Section 3.3.2; pp. 10-11, Section 4.2 and Table 3).

No eligible across_people homogenization measure is reported: Table 2 diversity is a participant assessment of tool performance, while Table 3 functional diversity concerns the functions of an individual product (pp. 6-8, Sections 3.3.1-3.3.3; p. 11, Tables 2-3).

Appendices A-D are referenced for the Combined questionnaire, prompt codebook, rater agreement details, and prompt strategies, respectively, but are absent from the stored PDF, which ends with references. The form accurately discloses this limitation (p. 8, Sections 3.3.3-3.3.4; p. 11, Sections 4.2-4.3; pp. 17-20, References).
This is an original experimental report, not a synthesis; no pooled estimate, confidence interval for a pooled estimate, or meta-analytic study count requires extraction (pp. 4-11, Sections 3-4).
summary: The stored arXiv v1 reports a randomized experiment with 20 recruited designers and 40 rated designs, so it belongs in the two-screener pipeline but fails the 50-person core threshold. The quoted Midjourney results and source version are correct; corrections concern four omitted output outcomes, the unreported analyzed-person denominator, and incomplete timing and contrast fields.
